chapter: Philadelphia, Atlantic City and the war years
title: Bardu Ali's band at the Club Paradise, Atlantic City, and Philadelphia
summary: Bardu Ali fronted an eleven or twelve piece band for the Club Paradise season, then took a smaller band to Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, then you go to -- according to (unintelligible) you go to Philadelphia for three years.
Yeah, I was in Philadelphia, worked Gaines there with Charlie Gaines.
What made you do that?
Well, we went -- we left New York with (unintelligible) used to be the front man for Chick Webb when they were at the Savoy, and Bordu formed his own group because he had --
What's his name?
Bardu Ali, yes.
Oh, yes, Bardu Ali.
So he wanted a band to take, open at the Club Paradise where Charlie Johnson used to work years ago. So by him being -- naturally, his brother was there.
This was in Philadelphia?

No, this was in Atlantic City. And we took the band each -- to New York, organized there's a band in New York. We rehearsed and went to Atlantic City, played the Season, and then we left Atlantic City and went to Philadelphia.
Well, how big a band was this?
He had -- he had 11 pieces, 12 pieces there in Atlantic City.
And who was the leader?
Bardu.
Well, I mean he fronted it, but who was like the straw boss. I mean you didn't know --
Well, of course, he didn't know that much about the --
Music --
-- music, you know, but piano player used to work with Erskine Hawkins was our pianist, and --
(Simultaneous remarks)
He got out of -- from Newark, New Jersey. And the band was mixed up with New Yorkers and some boys from New Jersey. Newark,
Well, this one that worked with
Erskine Hawkins, I mean he had -- I mean he had Avery Parrish. Then he had Ace --
It wasn't Avery. It was this boy before Avery.
Before Avery?
Yeah, Duke -- name was Duke. I've forgotten Duke's last name, very good piano player, though. I think Avery had left the band then.
Well, you had Ace Harris, didn't you, Erskine Hawkins and Ace Harris later? And -- oh, I don't know. Yeah, I guess Avery left around '40 something, yeah.
Yeah, because this boy didn't stayed with Erskine too long, Duke didn't.
(Simultaneous remarks)

Very good piano player. He had a lot of heavy shows at the Club Paradise, and we played on them shows, dance music too. And we went to Philadelphia, and they broke -- the band was about seven pieces there, and because Bardu didn't was in front of it.
Well, where did you work in Philly?
Well, I worked out there to different country clubs, and I worked with Charlie Gaines.
(Simultaneous remarks)
I meant when you took -- when this
band went to Philly with Bardu.
Well, they brought -- then they brought the band down, about eight pieces, very nice job.
